newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni jumps on GDR rumours.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni jumps on GDR rumours.

text.p: Shares of Komercni Banka, the largest Czech commercial bank, jumped early on the Prague Stock Exchange on Friday, spurred by rumours that the ceiling on the number of shares the bank could issue through global depositary receipts (GDRs) had been raised.
Komercni shares rose 52 crowns at the bourse's daily price fixing, and by 10.00 GMT had risen 102 crowns to 1,850.
Last year the central bank approved the issue of Komercni GDRs to a total volume of 10 percent of its equity.
The bank was rumoured to have asked the central bank, which must approve the sale of any Czech banking shares to foreigners, to raise the limit to 12 percent.
"Judging by the increased demand, it looks as though speculative investors are accepting the rumour and trying to get Komercni shares," said one foreign trader.
"There has been a big differential between the two (the price between shares and the GDRs) recently, and they are looking to later convert the shares into GDRs," he added.
Komercni GDRs were trading on the London Stock Exchange on Friday at the equivalent of 1,943 crowns.
Komercni initially converted 3.2 percent of its shares into GDRs for foreign investors, and has gradually increased the amount through subsequent coversions.
Komercni has not said how much of the 10 percent limit it has used. The GDRs are held by the Bank of New York.
Neither central bank officials nor Komercni officials were immediately available for comment.
The Komercni GDRs have no voting rights, and the issue of the securities has not raised the bank's basic capital.

A Komercni official was quoted in the local media in February as saying that if the limit were raised, shares would come from the open market and not the state's holdings in the bank. The state still holds 48.7 percent in Komercni.
